questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

__
 
• **‘Fastly’** is **not correct.**
 
• The word** ‘fast’ is used in the same form in adjectives and in adverbs.**
 
• Generally, we **add ' ly' to the adjectives to change them into adverbs.**
 
• But there are certain words that can be used **as adjectives as well as adverbs without adding 'ly'.** **Eg:** ‘ fast, straight, enough, etc. ‘
 
• **Examples-** * • He ran fast. (adverb)*

* •They like fast cars and expensive restaurants. (adjective)*

So, the right sentence is**:** *The birds flew fast above us as we stood on our terrace.__*

The correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said, “I can play the guitar pretty well.”

options.text: She said that she can play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she would play the guitar pretty well
She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she plays the guitar pretty well.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech** and we need to convert it to** indirect speech.**
 
• When we change a direct speech to indirect speech, we must follow these **rules:**

​ **•** The reporting verb** 'said' **remains unchanged.

 **•** The** inverted commas ("...")** are replaced with the conjunction **'that'** to show the indirect speech.

 **•** **A comma (,)** that is added after the direct speech part, **should be removed** in the indirect speech.

 **•** The modal **'can'** changes to **'could'.**

 **• 'I'** changes to **'she'.**

 
• Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

Hence, The Indirect speech is- ***She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.***

questions.question: When f(x) = 15x³ – 14x² – 4x + 10 is divided by (3x + 2), then the remainder is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Remainder Theorem, if a polynomial f(x) is divided by (ax + b), the remainder is f(−b/a).

Here, dividing by (3x + 2) means we substitute x = −2/3 into f(x).

f(−2/3) = 15(−8/27) − 14(4/9) − 4(−2/3) + 10

f(−2/3) = −40/9 − 56/9 + 24/9 + 90/9 = 18/9 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Polynomial f(x) = 15x³ − 14x² − 4x + 10

Divisor = 3x + 2

**Formula Used:**

Remainder Theorem: If f(x) is divided by ax + b, the remainder is f(−b/a).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let 3x + 2 = 0

⇒ 3x = −2

⇒ x = −2/3

⇒ Substitute x = −2/3 in f(x) to find the remainder:

⇒ Remainder = 15(−2/3)³ − 14(−2/3)² − 4(−2/3) + 10

⇒ Remainder = 15(−8/27) − 14(4/9) + 8/3 + 10

⇒ Remainder = −40/9 − 56/9 + 24/9 + 90/9

⇒ Remainder = (−40 − 56 + 24 + 90) / 9

⇒ Remainder = 18 / 9

⇒ Remainder = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remainder Theorem

When a polynomial p(x) is divided by a linear polynomial (x − a), the remainder is equal to p(a).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial p(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if p(a) = 0. This is a special case of the remainder theorem.

Polynomial Division

Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder, where the degree of the Remainder is strictly less than the degree of the Divisor.
</p
